title: Pentagon Gives UAP Whistleblowers A Legally Protected Pipeline
site_name: 2oceansvibe News | South African and international news
excerpt: The Pentagon has waived secrecy-agreement penalties for authorised UAP disclosures to its PURSUE review team.
content:
[Image: CC]

The Pentagon has given current and former military insiders a legally protected route to report classified UFO information, removing one of the penalties that could keep witnesses quiet. The route, however, leads to a government review team rather than straight onto the public internet.

The US Department of War announced the targeted waiver on Monday, 14 September, as part of the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters, mercifully shortened to PURSUE. It covers serving and former military personnel, civilian employees and contractors who have held access to relevant National Defense Information.

Under the new rule, those people may give protected information directly to designated PURSUE representatives without triggering civil or administrative enforcement provisions in Non-Disclosure Agreements or Special Access Program Indoctrination Agreements signed in the United States.

That is a tightly drawn permission. It does not authorise an insider to post classified files or hand protected material to anyone outside the existing lawful disclosure channels.

Instead, the department says disclosures will enter a pipeline for systematic review, security assessment and possible declassification. Newsweek describes the change as an attempt to remove fears about legal liability, lost security clearances and administrative punishment that have discouraged people with knowledge of alleged UAP programmes from speaking.

Trump ordered federal departments and agencies on 19 February to begin identifying and releasing records connected to alien life, unidentified anomalous phenomena and UFOs. The Pentagon says that job involves dozens of agencies and tens of millions of records, many of them still on paper.

PURSUE released its first batch on 8 May and its fifth on 7 August. By Tuesday, the official archive listed 375 files from agencies including the FBI, NASA, the CIA and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence.

Those files are not proof of extraterrestrial visitors. The department labels them unresolved cases, which means the available evidence is not sufficient to establish what was observed. Some entries contain videos or photographs, while others include witness accounts and digital reconstructions.

The waiver could still produce material that never reaches the public because national security restrictions remain in place. Its significance is more practical: authorised officials can now hear protected accounts without the source automatically breaching the secrecy agreement that granted access in the first place.

Whether that produces startling evidence or another warehouse of ambiguous lights depends on who comes forward, what can be verified and what the government ultimately clears for release. For the first time under PURSUE, the people closest to classified UAP material have an expressly protected door through which to enter.

[Sources: US Department of War & Newsweek]
